description: Classify benign and malignant breast lesions using mammographic metadata, feature selection, ensemble learning, and tabular machine learning

config.rationale: Test literature-mentioned voting with two diverse registered learners.
research_basis: ATwo-Stage Ensemble Feature Selection and Particle Swarm Optimization Approach for Micro-Array Data Classification in Distributed Computing Environments

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: The dual-branch neural network integrates ultrasound images and clinical data to improve PT classification accuracy.
evidence_records.paper_title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Phyllodes Tumor Classification from Ultrasound and Clinical Data
evidence_records.source_excerpt: We developed a dual-branch neural network that extracts and fuses features from ultrasound images and patient metadata from 81 subjects with confirmed PTs.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: Class-aware sampling and subject-stratified 5-fold cross-validation improve model robustness by addressing class imbalance and data leakage.
evidence_records.paper_title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Phyllodes Tumor Classification from Ultrasound and Clinical Data
evidence_records.source_excerpt: Class-aware sampling and subject-stratified 5-fold cross-validation were applied to prevent class imbalance and data leakage.

evidence_records.method: ConvNeXt and ResNet18 as image encoders
evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: ConvNeXt and ResNet18 are optimal image encoders for multimodal PT classification, achieving high AUC-ROC and F1-scores.
evidence_records.paper_title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Phyllodes Tumor Classification from Ultrasound and Clinical Data
evidence_records.source_excerpt: Among six image encoders, ConvNeXt and ResNet18 achieved the best performance in the multimodal setting, with AUC-ROC scores of 0.9427 and 0.9349, and F1-scores of 0.6720 and 0.7294, respectively.

evidence_records.method: Weight Predictor Network with Feature Selection (WPFS)
evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: WPFS reduces the number of learnable parameters and performs feature selection to improve performance on small sample tabular biomedical data.
evidence_records.paper_title: Weight Predictor Network with Feature Selection for Small Sample Tabular Biomedical Data
evidence_records.source_excerpt: In addition to the classification network, WPFS uses two small auxiliary networks that together output the weights of the first layer of the classification model.

evidence_records.method: Weight Predictor Network with Feature Selection (WPFS)
evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: WPFS achieves better performance than standard and recent methods on tabular biomedical data with small sample sizes.
evidence_records.paper_title: Weight Predictor Network with Feature Selection for Small Sample Tabular Biomedical Data
evidence_records.source_excerpt: We evaluate on nine real-world biomedical datasets and demonstrate that WPFS outperforms other standard as well as more recent methods typically applied to tabular data.

evidence_records.method: Weight Predictor Network with Feature Selection (WPFS)
evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: The feature selection mechanism in WPFS enhances model performance and offers insights into the learning task.
evidence_records.paper_title: Weight Predictor Network with Feature Selection for Small Sample Tabular Biomedical Data
evidence_records.source_excerpt: Furthermore, we investigate the proposed feature selection mechanism and show that it improves performance while providing useful insights into the learning task.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: nnU-Net can achieve near-human-level performance for 3D segmentation of the uterus and uterine tumors with fewer than 150 annotated images.
evidence_records.paper_title: Developing a Machine Learning-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Uterine Tumor Imaging
evidence_records.source_excerpt: We applied nnU-Net and explored the effect of training set size on performance by randomly generating subsets with 25, 45, 65 and 85 training set images.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: Radiomic features can distinguish between benign and malignant uterine tumors with an F1-score of 0.53 [0.45, 0.61] and between degenerated leiomyoma and leiomyosarcoma with an F1-score of 0.80 [0.80, 0.80].
evidence_records.paper_title: Developing a Machine Learning-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Uterine Tumor Imaging
evidence_records.source_excerpt: We evaluated the ability of radiomic features to distinguish between types of UT individually and when combined through feature selection and machine learning.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: Machine learning classifiers using radiomic features can achieve F1-scores of 0.53 [0.45, 0.61] for benign versus malignant classification and 0.80 [0.80, 0.80] for degenerated leiomyoma versus leiomyosarcoma classification.
evidence_records.paper_title: Developing a Machine Learning-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Uterine Tumor Imaging
evidence_records.source_excerpt: Classifying UTs based on radiomic features we identify classifiers achieving F1-scores of 0.53 [0.45, 0.61] and 0.80 [0.80, 0.80] on the test set for the benign versus malignant, and degenerated LM versus LMS tasks.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: The proposed model uses a Majority Voting Classifier to combine multiple machine learning models for enhanced classification performance.
evidence_records.paper_title: ATwo-Stage Ensemble Feature Selection and Particle Swarm Optimization Approach for Micro-Array Data Classification in Distributed Computing Environments

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: The proposed model incorporates Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) as part of the feature selection process.
evidence_records.paper_title: ATwo-Stage Ensemble Feature Selection and Particle Swarm Optimization Approach for Micro-Array Data Classification in Distributed Computing Environments

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: The proposed model includes Logistic Regression as one of the base classifiers in the ensemble.
